pr_title: [VideoPlayer] fix conditions for forced PGS/VobSub subtitles
pr_body:
## Description
[VideoPlayer] fix conditions for default enable forced PGS/VobSub subtitles

Fix https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/26050

## Motivation and context
In very specific circumstances are displayed by default wrong forced subtitle track and is not possible disable.

See: https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/26050 and forum https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=379599

This is because stream selection algorithm only picks the "best" track, based on user settings preferences, all available tracks and selected audio language, etc. but always ends up selecting one track (even when is disabled and not visible). 

Since the selected track is parsed to read possible PGS / VobSub forced subs (individual forced flag inside the stream) is possible displays forced subs on unexpected language (not selected language and not matching with audio language).

However, this only happens under very rare conditions: subtitles are all marked as forced (inside stream) and there is no normal or forced subtitle track in the same language as the audio.

New additional condition is audio language match when subtitle track only is opened for possible forced subs (the track has not been explicitly selected for any other reason).

NOTE: 
This modification only affects the conditions to "default enable" subtitle tracks. User always can change subtitles later from context playback menu i.e: enable other track or or maybe the same track that was not activated due to the changes in this PR.

## How has this been tested?
Runtime Windows x64 with prepared samples in https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/26050#issuecomment-2532290029

## What is the effect on users?
Prevent forced subtitles from being displayed in an unexpected language (not selected language and does not match the audio language).

pr_comments:
Simplified the logic as at end "visible" flag value contains the info of if subtitle "is relevant" with current settings.

Also added other code fragment to apply same logic when subtitle visibility changes during playback (user selects another track or toggles current on/off). Now works the same not only at open stream but when user changes settings.

e.g. subtitle is enabled because is the default in MKV container (or due user settings) and contains forced PGS subtitles in the stream. If user disables it from contextual menu and forced subtitles are in other language subtitle is closed. Instead if audio and subtitle is in the same language not closed but only displayed forced PGS subtitle lines (not all subtitles).

Example:

a PGS stream contains 1500 regular subtitles and 20 forced.

**case A: subtitle language is same as audio language**
stream enabled --> displayed 1500 + 20
stream disabled --> displayed only 20 

**case B: sub language is different as audio language**
stream enabled --> displayed 1500 + 20
stream disabled --> displayed 0

NOTE: the case B usually only happens when subtitle is "accidentally selected" because not exist better option (same language as audio or user setting language or forced flag in container, etc). In these conditions the stream is default disabled, then even if contains forced subtitles, none is displayed.
I'll merge it on Friday if no one objects.

> if (!visible && !g_LangCodeExpander.CompareISO639Codes(stream.language, as.language))

I'm running out of free time to investigate well,
my concern is that this change causes the overlay codec to running in memory even when not needed,
with it the whole parsing and rendering system (despite the latter being interrupted) as little as it affects the resources of a device

it is not possible to find a way to limit this to image formats (PGS/VobSub) only, and not applied to all subtitles formats?

I commented in #26050 about that type of solution.
VP and the GUI assume that a subtitle track is always loaded and this breaks the assumption and has consequences.
Very simple repro: play the sample, press T or enable subs with the OSD > nothing happens, instead of having the sub appear.

I sort of understand what the message handling in PLAYER_SET_SUBTITLESTREAM_VISIBLE is supposed to do, but it has the same problem, it turns off but doesn't turn back on.

it's low priority for me - and those subs are broken in the first place, but seems to me that it's in the overlay rendering that something should be done. Honour the SetEnableStream or compare language.

> my concern is that this change causes the overlay codec to running in memory even when not needed,

It's the opposite: now one subtitle stream is always open. 

With the PR subtitle stream is closed when not needed (not visible and not candidate for forced subtitles).

> With the PR subtitle stream is closed when not needed (not visible and not candidate for forced subtitles).

I think this PR better be on standby until i or someone else, finds time for a good review,
because i see that this behavior is applied to all subtitle formats which i don't find so correct

issue_context.title: Cannot Disable Forced PGS or VOBSUB Subtitles
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
When the Forced flag embedded in PGS or VOBSUB subtitles stream is set to true, it is not possible to disable them during playback in Kodi. Trying to set the forced flag in the container to false (mkv for example), has no effect as the embedded flags in the stream seem to override the container flags.

This issue has been reported on the forum here... https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=379599
It is accepted that the streams in the sample file are incorrectly flagged as forced, but Kodi should still allow a user to enable/disable them.


## Expected Behavior
Allow forced subtitles to be toggled on or off.



## Actual Behavior
Forced subtitles cannot be disabled.



## Possible Fix
--



### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. From the forum thread, download the sample file in post#16 (if the links have expired, let me know as I will hold onto the sample for a few weeks.)
2. Play file and try to disable subtitles.
3.


### Debuglog
Nil

Nil

comments:
In that specific case the problem comes from the existence of forced sub lines inside all sub tracks. It's a special capability of the vobsub/pgs formats, and in this case looks like an error in dvd authoring.
Unlike the usual track forced flag, already well controlled by various settings.

Even though none of the sub languages match the audio language, the first track is still added as stream to the demuxer (as hidden, because of no language match and not considered relevant). However the forced flag on the individual sub "lines" bypasses the hidden status and the wrong language forced subs are displayed.

I'm not sure where a change needs to be done without breaking the forced flag of individual pictures of vobsub/pgs.
In case of language match (or maybe undefined sub language) it's ok to display the forced subs and that was a long-time request of users when it was added (movies like Avatar and navi dialog apparently)

@CastagnaIT you have a better understanding of the big picture for subs and your PR #25813 comes close to that logic, maybe you have ideas?
sample can be made available in Slack if expired in forum
yeah i saw, but this week im too busy i have little time

i investigated,
there is a little difference between subtitle formats:
- PGS format: the flag "forced" when set in to the metadata means that a subtitle must be always shown, regardless of the user subtitle settings (yes also language dosnt matter)
- VOBSUB format: a "forced" flag is not intended as a mandatory to display, such as PGS, since its optional the flag can be also ignored (user controlled)

for the PGS use case Kodi currently do the right things, so mandatory force to show subs,
but for VOBSUB IMO the best thing is ignore "forced" flag
i will push a PR soon

> It is accepted that the streams in the sample file are incorrectly flagged as forced, but Kodi should still allow a user to enable/disable them.

streams in the sample file are incorrectly flagged as forced --> this is the point
Kodi should still allow a user to enable/disable them --> No, cannot be disabled with a setting, which is why they are called **forced**.

BUT subtitles should only be played if they correspond to the **same language as** the selected **audio**.

This seems also reproducible in Blu-Ray PGS subtitles:

I prepared two test streams (m2ts) to avoid possible interference with MKV container flags as the issue is related to internal forced flag of stream (not container).

The two streams are:

Only one audio (spa) and only one PGS subtitle (all individual subtitles with forced flag enabled)

The only difference is language of PGS:

```
stream_1: 
audio --> spa
sub   --> spa

stream_2:
audio --> spa
sub   --> eng 
```

This should be tested with Kodi Settings / Player / Language / Subtitles / Preferred subtitle language / Only forced

In these conditions is expected that only the stream_1 (`EO_dts-spa_pgs-spa(cut).m2ts`) displays subtitles as sub language match audio language.

But the two test streams displays forced subs (this is the bug).

NOTES: 
The subtitles are out of sync due cutting small samples to upload but is not relevant.
The PGS subtitles are the same (two in Spanish) but what counts is the language in which they are labeled.

https://www.mediafire.com/file/fpr129sf4jt1qfq/Test_PGS_forced.zip/file

~~The stream must be opened to retrieve the language so closing an undesirable track later seems unavoidable.~~
never mind that, reading the code is not enough I'll step through it later. Are those pre-lambda function of sorts?

Tracks were prioritized already based on the settings (hidden in the m_SelectionStreams.Get()) so only the highest priority track is opened.
Given that I'm not sure using the "forced only" language setting makes sense, but I'm not too clear on what it's supposed to do in the first place as a language choice.
It interacts and maybe conflicts with the player setting subtitles on/off available during playback in the OSD.

With unknown audio or unknown sub language (or both unknown) I think the stream should remain open. The track is the highest priority sub, meaning that a better language match was not available. It's not the same as a known different language.

But the vobsub/pgs in-stream forced flag and the track-level forced flag don't necessarily need the same thing.

Did I miss unit tests that would show the current behavior and expectations?

if you want that stream selection take the full control
just avoid set this var for subtitles

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/c1d02983a9819e8721db3f2d1933fb16816c3611/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDCodecs/Overlay/DVDOverlayCodecFFmpeg.cpp#L274

No, this variable controls if individual subtitles inside a stream are forced or not (can be all forced / all not forced / some forced). If  ignored this variable not differentiate anymore.

Stream selection determines which stream opens. Currently ALWAYS one stream is opened (even if not displayed).

With proposed diff, stream selection determines which stream opens (with the same priorities) but in very determined cases may decide do not open any.

I played with something similar, except inside the loop in order to avoid opening the stream and adding variables as your patch.

Both ways lead to an existing problem of the GUI: it shows the first sub as selected in osd or stream selection dialog even when disabled (because not relevant) or not loaded (fix for this issue) and the subtitle on/off toggle don't work normally until the sub is changed.
In theory the stream selection should be where the issue is fixed, but don't know how much work to take care of the gui.
As opposed to filtering the forced sub flag somewhere in the overlay (not as good, not the correct layer I think)
